node.name: Yale Forest Forum Fall 2026 Speaker Series: Unlocking Forest Sector Innovation: The Practice and Potential Pathways to Scaling Up
node.descriptionText:
September 3 – December 10, 2026

Exploring the practice and pathways to scaling up forest sector innovation is vital because global forest use and demand for wood and non-wood forest products are rising rapidly, affecting billions of people and putting pressure on forest ecosystems. At the same time, deforestation, unsustainable harvesting, and climate-change-driven stressors like wildfires and pests threaten forests’ health and resilience, creating urgent and sometimes competing management needs. Supporting and improving innovation can help reconcile these pressures by enabling sustainable forest management and community benefits, while filling gaps in awareness and research —especially beyond technology-centric, Western-focused perspectives — so effective solutions can be created, adopted, and scaled.

This fall 2026 Yale Forest Forum speaker series will explore the opportunities, challenges, and pathways that exist and are emerging in forestry innovation. This series will highlight speakers across a wide variety of forest research institutions, practitioner settings, and geographies. The series is developed and supported by members of the International Union of Forest Research Organizations’ (IUFRO) Scaling-Up Science-based Forest Sector Innovation Task Force and their broader networks.

Join us every Thursday from September 3 to December 10, from 12-1 p.m. U.S. ET. There will be no webinars on October 22 or November 26.

*Note: Sessions through October 29 will be held from 12-1 p.m. EDT (GMT-4). Beginning November 5, sessions will be held from 12-1 p.m. EST (GMT-5). 

The series is free and open to the public. Each session will be recorded. We will offer certificates of attendance for CEUs for foresters and practitioners who attend the live webinars. Please email yff@yale.edu(link sends e-mail) for further information.

node.name: Writing a Research Paper from A to Z in the Humanities and Social Sciences Series
node.descriptionText:
This 5-part series will walk you through drafting, refining, and submitting your fall 2026 research papers in the humanities or qualitative social sciences. Whether you’re writing a course paper, conference talk, or academic article, you will hone your craft as a research writer, work on developing a flexible and reflective writing process, and experiment with different ways to contribute to an academic conversation while retaining your voice. The 5-session structure is designed to help you make steady progress, submit your paper on time, and build a foundation of skills for your future writing projects. The sessions include:

Part 1: Drafting Your Initial Questions & Starting to Read & Write (Tue, 10/6)
Part 2: Finding Your Problem Collective & Writing an Ethical Lit Review (Tue, 10/13)
Part 3: Developing a Critical-Curious Stance and Voice (Tue, 10/27)
Part 4: Honing Your Argument and Paper Structure (Tue, 11/3)
Part 5: Revising & Editing (Tue 11/10)

Intended audience: GSAS and professional school students in the humanities and qualitative social sciences

node.name: Nurses Meeting the Moment, ANHE’s 2027 Conference: Submit Abstract
node.descriptionText:
Kicking off on March 25, 2027, the Alliance of Nurses for Healthy Environments (ANHE) will host Nurses Meeting the Moment: Healing, Advocating & Mobilizing for Planetary Health.

Over four weeks, this virtual conference will bring together nurses, students, educators, researchers, and environmental health leaders to build the knowledge and skills needed to advance healthier people and a healthier planet. Conference sessions will take place on March 25, April 1, April 8, and April 15, 2027.

SUBMIT AN ABSTRACT:
We are now accepting poster and presentation abstracts for the 2027 conference. Abstracts should align with the conference theme and its subthemes of Ethics, Health, Advocacy, and Collective Action. The submission deadline is December 1, 2026.

Students and practicing nurses should review the guidelines specific to their submission category before completing the shared abstract submission form. Student submissions may highlight projects across nursing education, research, advocacy, sustainability, community engagement, and related areas. Practicing nurses may submit work spanning research, evidence-based practice, nursing education, clinical practice, leadership, advocacy, policy, and community partnerships.

node.name: Dissertation Writing as Practice Series
node.descriptionText:
This series provides dissertation writers with the structure, resources, and creative outlets to design and maintain a sustainable approach to writing. We will explore effective practices for pacing your dissertation writing while helping you overcome common writing blocks and find balance in your writing life. During each weekly live workshop session, we will engage with a relevant theme, discuss your writing practice and progress, and complete low-stakes reflective and creative activities to build your writing momentum. Invigorated by poetry, art, and other creative inspirations, and supported through discussion boards and supplementary resources, we will help you craft a writing practice to help you maintain, and even enjoy, a PhD writing life. 

As part of the resources offered in this series, students will receive access to tutorials on how to try Scrivener, a software program for organizing writing and brainstorming. Students who attend at least four of the six sessions will receive a free, lifetime Scrivener license.

The weekly session themes are:  

1. Time Management and Dissertation Planning (10/27)
2. Crafting a Holistic Dissertation Writing Practice (11/3)
3. Working through Distractions and Procrastination (11/10)
4. Writing through Imposter Stress (11/17)
5. Hanging up on Perfectionism and Demoralization (12/1)
6. Assessing Process & Progress + Long-View Spring Semester Planning (12/8)

Intended Audience:  ABD PhD students from all disciplines who have begun writing their dissertation.

node.name: 2027 Untold Stories of Global Health Contest
node.descriptionText:
Do you know an important global health story that’s been overlooked by the media and deserves special notice? CUGH and Global Health NOW from the Johns Hopkins Bloomberg School of Public Health are pleased to announce the 2027 Untold Stories of Global Health Contest. The contest is designed to give a platform to important but underreported global health stories. You are invited to nominate an issue you feel deserves urgent attention. The best nominations focus on a specific issue in a specific location and should include available data and evidence, as well as contact information.

Submit your nomination, with a short (150-word) statement describing the story and why it deserves more coverage and support. GHN will select two winning stories to cover and appear in GHN. The two winners will receive free registration to CUGH2027.

node.name: The Global Lens Forum: Reflections in Global Health
node.descriptionText:
This annual contest provides an opportunity to submit reflections about global health education, research, and practice. The goal of the contest is to foster a culture of self-analysis, critical reflection, and cultural humility within the global health community. Submissions may be a written essay, art, photograph, video, or may be multimedia. Submissions will be reviewed by a panel and may be submitted in English or Spanish. Top submissions will be awarded free registration to attend the CUGH 2027 conference in Peru as well as a small monetary award.

Submit a reflection and view additional information here.

Submission Deadline: November 22, 2026

Contact Jenny Baenziger, MD (jbaenz@iu.edu) for questions.

The annual Global Lens Forum is co-sponsored by: CUGH, Child Family Health International, Indiana University Center for Global Health, Loyola University Chicago Center for Community and Global Health, and University of Pittsburgh Office of Global Affairs.

node.name: Food and Period Pantry Drive
node.descriptionText:
Upcoming Donation Drive for the YDS Food & Period Product Pantries!
 
Wait, YDS has a Food Pantry?
 
Yes! YDSG has kept a food pantry in the Student Kitchen in the Refectory since Fall 2021. The pantry is maintained through ongoing donations from students, staff, and our student government, and is available to any student. Additionally, leftover food from YDS events is frequently dropped off in the fridge. Keep a lookout for leftover food announcements on the YDS Facebook page, and feel free to stop by the pantry as needed.
 
Wait, YDS has a Period Pantry?
 
Yes! Free period products (pads, tampons, liners, etc.) are available in the all-gender bathrooms throughout the school year. These bathrooms are located inside of the library on the first floor, outside of Marquand Chapel, near the first-floor vending machines, and near the second floor common room.  Additionally, you can find products in the cabinets of the Student Kitchen in the Refectory. If you notice period products are running low in bathrooms, please notify us by scanning the QR codes located in all bathrooms where products are available.
 
Contribute to Food & Period Pantries, November 2nd-6th!
 
We welcome donations to the YDS Food and Period Pantries ANYTIME. Donations may be placed directly in the designated cabinets in the Student Kitchen on the 2nd Floor by the Refectory Dining Hall.
 
YDSG will also run a donation drive in the 2nd Floor Common Room, November 2nd-6th. Donations will be picked up at 2pm. Be on the lookout for an event invitation from YDSG!
 
For the Food Pantry, we appreciated non-perishable foods (i.e. canned goods, ramen noodles, crackers, granola bars) with a strong preference for individually wrapped goods; cases of water; paper dishes & utensils.
 
For the Period Pantry, we appreciate tampons, pads, liners, etc., for all flows.

node.name: Advanced Search Techniques
node.descriptionText: Learn skills to research like a librarian, including how to use "advanced search" techniques to find books and articles in Quicksearch.
node.descriptionHtml:
Have you ever felt overwhelmed by search results, or been stuck with almost none at all? This workshop will teach you how to research like a librarian, using advanced search strategies to narrow your results to find the best sources for your research. 

Attendees will learn how to: 

  • Navigate resource types in Quicksearch (books, articles, data sets, etc.) 
  • Apply filters to find more relevant results 
  • Identify terminology used by scholars (linked subjects, keywords, subject headings) 
  • Use operators AND, OR, and NOT to make your search more specific 

Audience: Undergraduate and graduate students in all disciplines. 

Workshop Incentive Program: Any student who attends at least 3 library workshops this semester will be eligible to receive a FREE Yale Library tote bag. Learn more.
